poems.title: A conversation among birds
stanzas:
a conversation among birds
Are you satisfied this morning / That’s a long sentence / Hark, here comes the dawn / that quiet scythe will slay this rural landscape

poems.title: A Wedding Toast
stanzas:
All I know, my friends
Is that terrible heartbreak
I would feel
When I left a place
that held me close
and made me feel
that this is this is
that there is there is
I can be
that when I left a place
Like that

There would be a curious heartbreak
A terrible heartbreak
A feeling of doubt and wonder and fear and loneliness and yes wonder again but so much doubt

But somehow what I feel now
Is just that wonder
With maybe a little more space for awe
Mixed in
Where that godforsaken heavy doubt used to be.
To you, my friends, all the love in the world.

poems.title: An Ode to Aspens
stanzas:
To me,
They’ve always been silent soldiers
Fighting against the slow erosion to entropy
It’s been hard watching them fall
These silent soldiers
My friends

I wish to spent eternity in their embrace
Let my matter become their matter
As it must
In the end

poems.title: And Now That We Walk in These Days of Light
stanzas:
And now that we walk in these days of light
Let the sun shine on our path

Heads held high
We walk

Heads held high
We walk

Days of light, days of pride, days of sun.

Here you come, here you come, here you come.
Be proud, child, for I am proud of you.

poems.title: Anuraag oh Anuraag
stanzas:
Anuraag oh Anuraag
Tell me where will you go?
You are caught and snared
Thrashing about
Will only cause your predicament to grow

Anuraag oh Anuraag
Oh now, what shall be done?
The chase is caught,
Secured you are mine,
As much as the one secures
The river which continues
to run

Anuraag, oh Anuraag.
Snared, you are to me. And so we shall sit,
And wait in discontent
To see what will be
Will be

poems.title: ariel
stanzas:
I'm sorry
i loved you once
and my love
made me pick you up
and spin you around

like if only I could spin fast enough
we could outspin the world

I loved you once
I hope you knew that
I hope you know that
I hope you know when we fell
we were spinning because I loved you
and thought I had to spin so fast
to keep you in my world.

poems.title: Blood Oh Once You Called to Me
stanzas:
Blood oh once you called to me
A siren song of betrayal
A defiance
A defiance
A defiance

Now you come unbidden
Leave you may,
May you linger,
headed or unheaded
Do we hurt less now?

Where does our pain go
When we grew
past
crying

poems.title: Burned Invitingly
stanzas:
He feels weird, hearing those words.
The pit grows in his stomach
and the scars on his wrist burn invitingly.
Were they treating Him right?

Take heed, innocent!
Kindness is a snare.
Spreads the legs and opens the mind.

Take heed, innocent!
Kindness is a card.
Dealt to some and played by few.

Take heed, innocent!
Kindness in his deck.
Will playing the card make him kind?

He had seen too many rapes.

That frame of reference you carry everywhere
Innocuous to the innocent
And Yet
But Yet
yet.

oh God kiss this mortal coil and reveal to me why

The scars on his wrist burned invitingly.

poems.title: California
stanzas:
California
There is a strange haze over the valley
It reminds me of home
Where the haze creeps where it should not be
And the valley sings and laughs
Boiling itself
in creeping death
And laughing all the while

Oh bruised, empty, raw dirt
Let us sing more your praises
Churn, churn, CHURN!
And grow life as I command.
Look mommy, how grown is your little prince.

poems.title: Dear Bottle
stanzas: I hope you are having a nice adventure without me
I miss you a lot
Be well, bottle.
May you make a new friend who loves you as much as I did.

poems.title: Delicate pieces before the end
stanzas:
To find beauty
In a streetcar
Or a bus
Full of black haired brown skinned children
Seated mischievously

Is no great shakes
Anymore
Look, Remember, Recreate,
The memories you wish you had
And this joy
Delicate pieces
Can be yours.

poems.title: Did You Know There Are Spiders with Only 5 Legs
stanzas:
Did you know there are spiders with only 5 legs
I met one this morning
the time when the bulbuls duet with the sparrows

Did you know there’s a pale pink before dawn
just a hint of pink
So hinting you could miss it or think you had a momentary affliction
A curse of having been in a room so green
Even the fairest of light seem pink by comparison

Did you know to remember the form
Fades

What will this boat be when the boats go home
What will happen to the 5 legged spider
What was this place before trees and nature conquered

Is it honor to play by the same rules
Is it honor to find the hole in the rules
Is it honor to evolve your own approach
Is it honor

when you realize you are the kind of fish
That can jump out of water
And fly

poems.title: Do You Miss Me
stanzas:
Do you miss me
Now that I hide
my heart
From you

Or maybe
you haven’t noticed, yet
Or maybe
you have, and you are indifferent
Or maybe
Or maybe
Or maybe

The world asked me if I wanted to call you today.
Multiple times.
I did not.

poems.title: Everyday I Can Spend
stanzas:
Everyday I can spend
in the company of those whom I love
I count a day thankful.

There will come a time, I know there will come a time, that our time will be lost in this and that, in what could be and what was,
there will be times when days are lost to what must be and what was.
That will be.
But today, I get to spend time with my lovers. My friends. My joys. My life, manifest in people.

Our health may not be for this world.
Our lives may not be for this world.
But help me if there is not tomorrow.
Help me if there is no memory before today.
Help me if what is today’s tomorrow is actually just today.

Today is a day in the company of those I love.
And lord love bless
So tomorrow be.

poems.title: Everytime you wink at me
stanzas:
Everytime you wink at me
I wonder if my heart skipped a beat
Or if I just forgot to breath
for a minute

I wonder if the excitement can bubble up my chest
Can you be so excited that you forget to breath
I think so,
I just did

poems.title: Everywhere I Turn
stanzas:
Everywhere I turn
In the flutter of the leaves and the remembrance of your laugh
Everywhere I turn
In the follow of your face and rememberance of a smile
Everywhere I turn

I see a world a little colder
A heart a little stiller and laughter little less.

poems.title: Falling in love with who I am vs who I could be
stanzas:
Falling in love with who I am
Is like the air
You can breath
When you've been without air
And you get the tiniest sip
Like that from a balloon
Not yet ready to yield up its original form

Falling in love with who I could be
Is like telling someone
About the sublime joy
Of being naked
under a waterfall
in the sun

When that someone
Has only ever known
The pale approximation
His brethren made
And called it bath.

poems.title: Freedom, Yet Unabridged
stanzas:
As my feet flew over
the expanse
Grey and long before me,
I panged in my stomach
Something long thought forgotten.

As my feet flew over
the expanse
Grey and long before me,
I looked and wondered
If I leapt, would the pang stay?

As my feet flew over
the expanse
Grey and long before me,
I thought to myself
Well at least, there is this.

poems.title: Glass Houses
stanzas:
Glass houses
We take so much time
To build our houses
A ledge here
A porch there

You would think we were going to live for eternity
And our house was meant to be our
Final solitude as the madness of age set in
And the weariness of routine
Comfort till death.

poems.title: Guadalajara
stanzas:
I feel blood and strife and fear
In this soil
I feel worry
In this heart

I see fear in the eyes
And in the way the plants grow
They seem
As though in wonder
As though in fear

What is that they say about the trees men make
Tall, sightless, reaching as did their ancestors, their forebears, those who had a time to live and a time to fall, in a way that these new trees don't have, anymore.
I wonder if i would feel the blood if I didn't know to search for it.

poems.title: Hark, My Love!
stanzas:
Hark, my love!
It’s a little tree
onto that hillside
Look at it glow,
sun chasing luminance
eyes chasing the sky

That tree don’t care one bit that its hill is a mountain
Made of cement and steel
And the labor of many men
Not the long labor of the tides
And the hills
And the rivers of ice
Calling their way home

It’s dancing now, in the morning wind
And every now and again some small glowing white shape
Deigns to join it
A ghost of ideas long past

Or clump of sand
Or plastic bag, the hubris of days long ago
At this distance, who can say
Dream, dream dream, little tree
Life and love be all you do

poems.title: Have you ever seen
stanzas:
Have you ever seen
Something so beautiful
As the world reflected in drops of dew
Hanging off a cedar

That saw your parents parents parents parents
Walk across this land
When the cedars still walked

A secret gift they gave up
When the people came to trouble them

poems.title: Have you watched creepers creep
stanzas:
Come watch creepers creep
See this dedication!

Trials and tribulations bear witness

Traversing hills
Traversing barriers

The most arduous of grounds

What dedication, you creepers
Evolved to find the smallest of holes
And use it to crumble all foundations.

poems.title: Hey you there, hey you here
stanzas:
hey you there
hey you here
we got stuck together somehow
your shoulder got caught in my shirt
your breath got caught in my air
is that mine or is that yours

poems.title: Hey you tree there
stanzas:
Hey you tree there it’s nice to see you today I didn’t know you knew so much about height and heights — I knew you knew about growth but it was only when I started to talk to this one part of you it told me about how we are always thinking about heights.
And how most of you doesn’t have to worry about heights — most of you gets to just grow and do its thing, be growing and be taller. Be trying to be ever taller. Responsible for the height, but not for worrying about it just growth growth growth.

Because of the other trees, you see, they have this way of coming in and like how — blocking the light, eating the soil, you can’t even find or make a grape of light, a square come to be a circle because 3d always renders weird in 2d, you think we meant to have our rings be this way? We were trying to just grow grow grow, and that made it much harder to worry about how we would render when you cut 2d segments out of us — we never dreamed we would be required to be snapshots in half, mandolin’d into the thinnest slices possible sometimes, because those are the things that show them they know how to really do it, how to win at life, show them they know how to cut, how to get themselves a tree.

Hey you tree I didn’t know what those gashes those gouges in your trunk came from are they a hurt from when you are young or are they a hurt from maintaining the base for all of the height you need to achieve to have a spot of light in this world.

Hey you tree I thought that was a little bit of poop that was on your bark on your trunk on your arm but what poop could stain a bark or a trunk or an arm of a tree? Is it a fungus my tree friend is that what left the scars the gouges not ants not termites not woodpeckers searching for a mate but was it a fungus that organism so mysterious how could something so small hold so much mystery, I hear its a story the elephant is asking its friends after it saw a mouse, have you ever seen an elephant actually frightened of a mouse, don’t say it too loud or they will hear and start hunting and cut down all of us trees oops I mean you trees the hills the grass the arms the trunks all to find the elephant hiding from those, you know it’s true you there tree my friend, you.

poems.title: His hair was curly
stanzas:
His hair was curly, and it smiled when he did.

His heart was too shy to let it relax, so it danced, motionless, and kept you from looking in his eyes.

His eyes were arresting, and chiseled by shadows. Makeup or fatigue, who could tell?

His eyes did not know how beautiful he was.

But his hair was curly. And it kept you from looking in his eyes.

When he spoke, sweet serenity stole your heart. Gone were those shadows!

Who was this sweet innocent, so pure, kind, naïve?

Oh, Lord, save this sweet innocent, so pure, kind, naïve.

After he spoke, purity troubled into silence.

After he spoke, he disappeared into silence.

He disappeared behind his eyes, touched by pain.

And behind his hair, so curly.

Languidly
it reached down.
Twining about
Relishing for the moment where
he might smile
and it might
put on
its wanton display
once more.

poems.title: How Can You Just Be Gone
stanzas:
How can you just be gone
That’s it
That’s the one by one
As we were born, so we will go
And the only ease may be if you ease into it
With an empty space
Kept a little away
Before the empty space
Comes to play with your heart.

I could move anything
I could see
Anything
but not this anything
Who knew

This what
This empty
This what
This empty
This
Space
Empty space

I will miss you my friend
And resent a bit this empty space
This space that was your empty space
This space that had bugs and friends and deep zest for life
You did well, I thought

Why did you just die
At my age
At our age
It’s not sexy anymore
Or notable, really
It’s just deeply sad.
Ouch

poems.title: I feel sad about endings
stanzas:
I feel sad about endings
It's in the existential sort of sad
Like when it's too humid for your hair
It's hard to keep brushing your teeth
Cause you're a fucking poet
You gotta be writing poetry while you're trying to fucking brush your teeth

I guess it's because every time something ends
Remind you, everything has to end
This may be your last time with these people
This might be your last time in this place
This might be the last time you are this person

One day will be a bitter version of yourself
You know this
We fight to ward off that day
All versions of ourselves
It's nice finding a mirror that actually lets us see ourselves

I feel sad, my sweet love
Come, won't you give me succor
I feel sad, my sweet lover
Come, let me home.

poems.title: I left my heart at home today
stanzas:
I left my heart at home today
and without heart
the chest feels strange
Uneasy
something was forgotten
Who was supposed to remember some parts of you
that you had forgotten of yourself.
maybe my heart is a person
Maybe my heart was a person

poems.title: I Listen
stanzas:
Is it better to know this is your last goodbye
Mutter words of encouragement
Suggestions of forlorn strength
Too little
Too late
Paltry nothings to fill
A silence

This time when the silence comes
There will be no escape
No respite on a beach
To mutter words of encouragement
Too little
Too late
Too soon
Too gone
The timing is never right until there is no time at all, amirite?
Nah man maybe it’s better

Let the guillotine come in the night
Sharp strokes and sharp blades
Exhaust not my precious store of hope.

poems.title: I saw something beautiful today
stanzas:
I saw something beautiful today
It gives me shivers to think of it
For to let yourself see beauty
Is a special gift
Not to be taken
By the giver
Or the gived.

And hark! Yes
For this was beauty
Clad and a shimmer of red
Brown against the sun
Resplendent agent of life
Oh Creator
I praise you
I salute you
What creations you have made.

I watch this boy come to end life
Or bring it
So innocent is wonder
So innocent is life
Oh, you shimmer of Red. Shimmer me brighter, you.
Shimmer me wonder, you.

Whether I die in peace is my choice.
Whether I die at all, maybe yours
God bless you
Child of creation
Child of wonder
Child of tears

poems.title: I Was Feeling Sorry for a Moth
stanzas:
I was feeling sorry for a moth,
Or flying ant,
Some creature without full understanding of its wings
I thought
As I watched it squirm yesterday. wings stuck in candle wax.

But today
the thought struck me.
Whose to say we aren’t the moth
Squirming next to certain doom
And it is the moth
Who is watching
And giving homage
Bearing sad witness
To our slow demise
With a composition
Of its own.

poems.title: I watch my hair
stanzas:
I watch my hair
Turn golden
In the reflection of my eyes

I wonder
that this dazzling array
Of reds and greens
Of Browns and oranges
Existed
Beneath (or should I say above)
My nose

And,
Fool that I was

I just went and called it all black.

poems.title: I watched a butterfly today
stanzas:
I watched a butterfly today
It was beautiful and orange
And had a certain way about it

Maybe it was the way it
Fluttered its wings
A daintiful wink
A debutante poised, posed
Ready.

As I passed by
Ensconced in perfect climate
I heard the slight thud
Of a delicate body
Caught in the draft of my passage.

poems.title: I Will Always Be a Poet
stanzas:
I will always be a poet
Without my hands I will be a poet
If you sand away my finger tips I will be a poet
If you shave my chest to expose my heart
With my blood I will paint you with poetry

poems.title: In my heart something called to the rain
stanzas:
In my heart something called to the rain
It had always called to the rain
In days before and days past
You know there's a lot of people who think fire was the gift of mankind
That taught us there was an us
But wonder

Conjecture the rain

Champion of life
Heretic before Dawn

Being Life's chartreuse-clad champion,
Of course you would say that,
You say,
Champion of life over destruction
Value-er of order over chaos
Of course you'd say that
You say.

To which I say

Watch the rain

And it will bring destruction down on your head
Watch the trees
And they will break your mountains
Watch the stones
And they will crush your plants
Even watch us burn
And be reborn, oak grow tall, pine grow fierce

I just say

Are you 90% fire or 80% water

And who lives better

But what is better

To the drowning man

Or burning man

Watch the rain.

poems.title: it used to be me
stanzas:
it used to be
it used to be me
writhing under you
or riding beside you

it used to be me
who made you
forget to wonder

it used to be.

me.

poems.title: one year on
stanzas:
It’s funny
Being apart from you
My husband

Funnier still
To call you that
My husband

And wonder about when we got to be
This age
With wonder
Still
But regret
too,
Sometimes

So let’s go
My husband

Let’s go together
Down the long roads
the deaths to come
And the joys
too
Sometimes

We started this journey
Long days ago
My husband

In Sadashivnagar
Under orange lights
And warm nights

So, let’s go to the mountains, my husband,
And the sun

And see what’s there when we wake up
If we wake up
From this dream without beginning or end

When was it, my husband?
Oh yes, the day I fell in love with you

21 is 21 is 21 is 21 until one day you can’t sleep
And have to wonder, my husband
Is this day like that day,
All over again

poems.title: Kashmir
stanzas:
As I look and wonder
‘Has such a thing been seen before’
I search
Memories mine own
Remembrance owned by others,
That which was before
(Or as I willed it to be)

But in the Truth
That which has to be done
Which will always be done
Will be here
Till time razes these mountains to the ground
And man builds new idols.

poems.title: Large objects exert a gravitational pull
stanzas:
Large objects exert a gravitational pull
The issue arises when the connection between objects start to exert its own gravitational pull
That thing which binds you to them is now alive with its own force
interlude/fun fact: gravity is the weakest of all fundamental forces. And some would say fundamental facts too.

What do you do for your fundamental forces
What about fundamental relationships
What about when the relationship matters more than the person
Arbitering justice, again.

poems.title: Late why so late
stanzas:
Late why so late.

Maybe we should have gone to the airport instead of napping.
But done.

The cab really smells.
Should I tip him 500 for driving so fast and tell him to go get the car cleaned?

I smile instead.

Are you flirting with me?
Is he just keeping me at the counter to dance his eyes a little longer and keep his breath intertwined a little a little a little.

10 min to discover check-in opens 24 hours before.

Make the humans bored and they will dance.
Privately.
In their head.
Let me fuck with you a little bit.

Could he have a metal watch bracelet?
is it a threat is it a threat is it a threat
But could he?

Make the humans bored and they will dance
Maybe not always in their head.
How’s your head
Let me love you a little bit.

poems.title: Let tomorrow come
stanzas:
Let tomorrow come for today has no brother
Let tomorrow come for today has no cousin
Let tomorrow come for that fear and heart of mine
that asked for today
when tomorrow is all we have.

poems.title: London
stanzas:
There’s a coldness in the air
I, me, mine! does not remember,
From this place
In that time,
before.

There’s a coldness in these people,
I remember,
In this place,
But it feels jagged now,
Full of icy points
Ready to rip
Tear
Cut you up
Not ice you out.

There’s a worry in faces,
They don’t look at you too long
they don’t know who they’re looking at
they are scared to look too long

to look
at the wrong
person.

You, my dark friend, might just be

A wrong
Person.

There’s a coldness in the air
And it is not just the air.

poems.title: Mama
stanzas:
Mama was what we called him
Because Masseur always seemed to harsh
Too far away a relation
For such a man who always kept us
so close to his heart

As our generation grew to up prominence
And demanded our due space
He shucked responsibilities well
and gracefully let go of center stage

He turned his eyes to making life
And made a space filled with love
Created harmony and beauty
Joy and accord
and a world that delighted
To all who came abound

Each day, each hour,
Each time we got to spend
a few minutes
On his terrace,
Or in his bar,

Or just a few moments of company,
As the sun set and we had
a single malt
Or a whiskey
That we had never before heard of
Or even before known existed.

Today let us unite in grief
For those who never knew him
And for those whose knowing was too short
But celebrate the days we knew him
And celebrate the steps we took together

You’ve gone into that gentle night,
Sweet mama, sweet father, sweet husband, sweet friend.
God keep you till we walk together again.

poems.title: Memories of tomorrow
stanzas:
I wonder,
will This be,
when I, tomorrow,
remember today?

As I stare
at the hazy notes of tomorrow,
and wonder
if they
emote today.

After all, the trees are there
before tomorrow,
and they will be
before my today,
so who,
Who am I to say?

poems.title: my friend who died
stanzas:
My friend who died
It's too bad
English has no imperfect
To talk about those things
That existed
And will exist
But.

poems.title: Not in my life
stanzas:
you can try to talk to me all you want
I will not speak to you
Not in my life
Not in my life

You can try to blackmail me all you want
I will not speak to you
Not in my life
Not in my life

Oh when you come this way
I know
You do not mean well
So please sir

Not in my life
Not in my life

My life is good
And pure
And happy
And I will fight to keep it that way

So please sir
Walk out that door
You will be

Not in my life
Not in my life

So get the hell out of my life
I know what comes
Of associating with filth
And I will not have it

poems.title: Oh that again I might see such beauty in my life
stanzas:
Oh that again I might see such beauty in my life

As a single flower
Opened and yet unmarked
Ungrieved by the world

poems.title: Oh the horror I say
stanzas:
Oh the horror I say
A finger on nicely chopped
Upon the cutting board
Emincer amongst the carrots
Perfectly outstretched
As though it too, was just another carrot
Was it a carrot?

poems.title: One Beautiful Moment
stanzas:
One beautiful moment

Where you don’t have to decide anything

You don’t have to do anything

The world has stopped

You can just be.

And feel veins on your fingers

Bring the slightly chilled blood

Back to your heart.
That, my friends, is the moment before death.

poems.title: One in community community community
stanzas:
One in a community or a community or a community

A Community speaks: Bataille tells us it is in death we find our people interchangeable.
In death we reveal their individuality.

Why should that collection of us, that star dust bound in that shape, deserve to be remembered,
the sand asks me, observing, sighing by, caught in a flick of wind and it's gone.

A Community speaks: Glissant asks can we be in relation to each other,
un-barred unbowed by grounding,
existent outside of a time.

Let opposition be left in two dimensions, advance, expand, grow. Become 3.

Can there be an us without a them?

A Community speaks, asks: how do I grow when you defined me to be a thing.
Is that thing meant to be, to change and grow?
How do I change when I exist only as a definition?
If I am outside of you, and you are outside of me,
who gets to say what I am?

Who chooses fascism?
Who chooses fear.

Was I stronger when I was a community bounded by fear?
Prohibitions, customs, duties and dues?

Exist. Live: My first commandment.
There was no qualifier. No but.

If you wanted me to die, I should have been a 100-year project. A 50-year project. A 10-year project.
If you wanted me to die, you should have told me when I would die when I was born.

poems.title: Out of Many, One
stanzas:
Out of many, one
Out of one, many.

Today:
There was joy, once.
There was life, once.
There was, once.

Kiss me love
I’m free.

Kiss me love
I’m free

Kiss me love
What more do you want
I’m fucking free.

poems.title: Out to play He calls them
stanzas:
Out to play He calls them
One, two, they come in a line
Chasing, what else?

Fish, fish come to me today
To your brothers we’ve paid dues
To your sisters we’ve given meals
Swim to me, swim to me, swim to me

One, two, they come in a line
One, two, they fly West.

poems.title: Park
stanzas:
I whisper to you
A story of today
Blond girls
Black wings
A whisper of red

This is a park
Our park

A place for forgotten gloves
And old dogs teaching new tricks and a delight of flowers
And laughter finding a new way to wonder

Next to

Fear is a spiral
And with each coil
It pulls tighter

Better to be lost in the crowd
Then followed alone
Or worse still
Seen to be alone

It whispers

Hauntingly. Breathily. A wizard's oratory come to tell its tricks

Do not enter
It says
Least you break the shackles
Of good
And right

A spy of red again
And I wonder
Am I finished
Or will I see more than a splash

A passing glance
And I'm compelled to change
Least my visage
So beautifully done
Freshly polished and precise
Doth offend thee

A scream
And I wonder
Do I have a purpose here
At all

Maybe art is purpose enough
On a sunny day
In a city that induces pain
To give you something
To make art
About.

A black car
and I'm gone.

poems.title: Platitudes of Suffering
stanzas:
For it is only in death,
that we shall lay down our Labors,
our Arms.
And only then
shall we say,
“Why yes, Sir! I am okay.”

Until then, Sir,
ask me not how I am.
For does breath not still shake my body?
Does my mind not still delight you?
So, Sir, ask me not how I am.

I am alive, yet.
And so my choice is made.
Platitudes of suffering serve no man.

poems.title: Sit let us listen to the sound of this moment
stanzas:
Sit let us listen to the sound of this moment
Watch the game board
See the leaves
The women and the dogs
The cars
The wind
And in the flowers
All that is today and will be
Tomorrow

poems.title: Social media is not the right place for grief
stanzas:
Social media is not the right place for grief
Some other place is more right
Maybe some place profound
Like temple
Or church
Or the divinity in choosing a temporary voicelessness

I'm not ready to move on
After 24 hours
I still persist
In this feeling
I chafe at your rules

Who are you to tell me how to grieve
Who are you to tell me

Is this all that becomes of us
Some shapes strung together in homage
A passing mark
On a bench, in a vibration, in a thought in a stone in a notion of remembrance

It's kind of freeing

poems.title: sometimes, a curious feel
stanzas:
There's a curious feel we feel, sometimes
It's a light pressure on the nose
A gentle warm pushing down
Coming from a place
Nestled between the eyebrows
(Or perhaps in them)
(Depending on their shape)
(Sizing)
(And general demeanor)

Oh my lord
There's a joy bubbling in my heart
That tells me
That joy that you find
In symmetry and perfectly formed spaces
Zoom out just a little
Or zoom in just a touch
Won't you be darned
If there ain't symmetry
And that goddamn blissful joy
In almost every second
Of every moment
Of every day
I think I've walked this fair green
(Okay so it's blue, but I'm a green man myself)
Fair green
Tiny round ball
In a big
Black
Sky

Did I remember to tell you
My nose
Is pleasantly warm

Did you know

I love you

poems.title: sometimes I feel cold
stanzas:
Sometimes
I feel cold when I think
Sometimes
I feel cold when I be with you
Sometimes
I know this is a betrayal of whom I aspire to be

Sometimes
I want a different game to play
Sometimes
I want to construct a different home
Sometimes
I feel like an intersection of regrets and what could have been

Sometimes
I am tired of being tired
Sometimes

poems.title: Sometimes I listen to these poets
stanzas:
Sometimes I listen to these poets
go on and on
about
the purest form of love
and joy
and I wonder

Is there a pure form of vomit too
or only these
intangible nouns
that we made up
one day
when confronted with
that thing
that stretched
our capacity for wonder.

poems.title: sometimes, the whole field a'quaver
stanzas:
Sometimes to watch the whole field a'quaver
Is to see leaves dancing a tiny dance
Feet so fast a'flutter
It's double time
Double speed
Double life

You wonder:
Am I moving slow?
Or is the whole world
A'flutter
A'quiver
A'wondering what things is.

poems.title: Song of Tomorrow
stanzas:
Sing to me, oh, Song of Tomorrow
Tell me the stories you once told
Of disasters foreshadowed
foreclosed before their chit came due.

Oh sing to me, you, Song of Tomorrow
Will you grow tall
Crookedly yearning towards the lights
That see you and beat you

Oh sing to me, you
Tell me, is it tomorrow?

It was my mistakes that drove you from this plane
Come back to me
Before tomorrow comes
And there are no more todays.

Grow tall
Expand your insides till you burst forth
A mirror of the older, reaching ever taller.

Oh, you, Song of Tomorrow,
Get out of here.
Today is enough
Today is all we can manage
Today is all we can need.

poems.title: Teental
stanzas:
teental
ta comes the first step, to greet sum and kiss it goodbye, assure it the cycle begins again
te comes the second step, likely alone in the sound scape, a perfect quarter away from the beat to come
te right foot again, are we floating now or chasing the beat
te left and the cycle is half done, this time we will be strong

who am I a dancer who can’t keep attention for 4 beats, where are we going to find heritage in a mélange of cultures, what search for heritage is this but someone to choose you to love you to tell you you are loved loved loved

ah left again, we’ve entered the back half, and if it was chogun we dance here has come the beat again, to ground us and remind us our math need be right every time
te right foot have you spoken as loud? Or 6th beat have you fallen soft, leaving the memory of the 4th and 3rd to leave a mark
te left again and we close in on home, sum, likely a foot away, unless this tihai has left us twisted and turned, math askew.
ta have we come home to you, sum? or is this a fake, a feint to remind the listener, watcher, life is a game, and nothing is what it seems.

poems.title: The Light Sings to Me in the Morning
stanzas:
the light sings to me in the morning
coos, really, a feather’s brush against my ears.

drrrrrrrrrrrrrrum, drrrrrrrrrum, drrrrrum.

But then it rains and I wonder about the birds

what do they think, when the rain falls without end, and hunger drives them forth from sanctuary?

What do they think, buffeted by wind and water, berated by flying bodies?

change or die, says the rain.

drrrrrrrrrrrum, drrrrrrrrrrum, drrrrrum.

soothed though I am by the contortions of these soft wet bodies on these cold hard surfaces

they drown out the birds.

drrrrrrrum, drrrrrrrrrrum, drrrrrrrrum

poems.title: The Mist
stanzas:
In the morning you can listen to the mist. It dies as it burns, little by little, slow by slow.

If you sit still and don't move your eyes you can see it fleeing.

It runs from the invading sun, hoping, wondering,
Thinking maybe today, maybe this day, even if I don't win, one of us will.

Their kiss is soft and cool on my skin, and tastes of a color I've never seen.

When I first came out I saw the drops of dew and wondered — is this? Will this be?

Then their bodies broke together, melded into ever bigger drops, and I remembered, oh this is the ocean, come to play in the air for a while.

Oh this is the ocean, least you forget who rules this world.

Oh this is the ocean, who taught you all life and fed you warmth, and left you craving another day, from the moment you left the ocean of your mother.

Till.

Till what may be.

till what may come.

poems.title: The sun kissed the mountains
stanzas:
The sun kissed the mountains
And by its sly caress
Peaks in harsh repose
I knew

Oh!
Today today today
By the grace of God
The babe of tomorrow has been born.

poems.title: There Comes a Point
stanzas:
There comes a point one chooses death.
And at that point,
You die.

Not from illness,
Not from stroke,
Not from despair,
Not from loss of blood.

It is that ebbing of the will to live that brings death.
That weariness that grows,
Deep in each cell,
And, leaves it asking,
“Why, again, today?”

poems.title: There Is a Soft Tingle I Feel
stanzas:
There is a soft tingle I feel
When grounded
Into the trees
And often my favorite tree
The biggest and oldest tree

But then do we count age after death?
A tree is a tree is a tree until it’s not
And then it’s dirt
Or some other pejorative
Depending on your fancy
And your society’s feelings about trees

This tree, though
Long dead, though it may be
This tree though
Its soft bark and slowly molding hardwood
From its heart, so soft and gentle
Once so hard and firm
Who’s to say who is the better version of itself? tree? society? Culture? You?
Life is and is and is until it’s not

Ouch, I say. this hurts my heart.
Ouch, I say. I wonder about tomorrow.

poems.title: These Days Are Gone
stanzas:
these days are gone
never can they return
who has hardened?
who softens, as they age?

Harden or rot, they say.

Harden or rot.
Let there be joy that it happened.

poems.title: These Water Nymphs
stanzas:
They come up from the River
Have you ever felt hands
So soft
So wet
So sweet

They kissed your lips as they went by
And looking back you saw
Their forever Why
Creator, Destroyer, bringer of the Day.

Oh, inversion, birth me again, they kissed across my lips

Oh inversion, these water nymphs.

poems.title: This growing older
stanzas:
This growing older
Wondering
If this goodbye is the last

Will the space that I feel
Which you occupied
And made warm
And friendly
Softly inviting
Ache
How do I remember you without this space

poems.title: thrum thrum
stanzas:
thrum thrum
what brings you to excitement today
my liege

remembered mistakes
affronts
ways sinned against you and yours
sinners escaped justice
by smilin a bit too cute
or wonderin a bit brave
or dreamin a bit too much

colors to express my unease
Violet is too gentle of a flower.
We need the harshness of purple, or red
Or a pink to show intestinal flesh and precluded winter

poems.title: Time in a Fig Grove
stanzas:
And he looked down the Long Years,
And the Grove grew and grew and grew
And then faded from view.

Then came a house.
Then a hill.
Then a stream.

And then he saw
A plant
Rooted in a climb of dirt
And the seed of the Grove
Once again, or before?
Who can tell.

Time has no master
And
    his
    hers
    its
            secrets are unending.

poems.title: To Be Alone
stanzas:
To be alone
with the mountains
As different than in the mountains
(a far more precarious place)
Is a special gift
that was designed on the 8th day

For those
who get lost
Sometimes
and wander
Wondering
if there is a place
For babies who like the snow
but not being too cold
And dreaming about green grass
on a different day

poems.title: To Flutter
stanzas:
To flutter
Is to act in that moment
after doing
When you have cocked the second arrow
And maybe the third
But you pause, a’wondering

Was right right?
Or did I let a tired calculus
tell me what was right
When I wasn’t sure
what was right or wrong

It’s a cold wind that blows from the north
Sends my heart a’flutter.

poems.title: To Know Me
stanzas:
To know me

Is to know joy
Because I laugh a lot
And I fall in love a lot
And sometimes it feels like one life
Is just too short

But then I couldn’t bear to do
Any of it again
So maybe it’s just long enough?

Kiss me and I’ll smile, because I love smiling
Love me, and I don’t know, we’ll see?
Love means a lot
And a lot of things to a lot of people

poems.title: To See Such Beauty
stanzas:
To see such beauty
To stand in a field
Or the side of a road
And think only
Why you, Orange
I didn’t know I had seen you before.

poems.title: To touch, in a way
stanzas:
To touch
in a way
gives remembrance
I don’t know
if I can take
Sometimes

poems.title: Today
stanzas:
We are past the morning of the small birds
Into the morning of the crows
Or is it ravens
The caw of one seems as harsh as the other
Though maybe there is more music in the one who takes me to rest

There’s an ache, the chronic sort of ache that brings weary, chases moments of calm allusion before it
I hear my time calling

Or maybe that’s just a phone
Missive
Urgent demanding of synchronization
Calling to my neighbor

Something to be heard, but not done
Something to be seen, but not done

What a gift, to be on an island.
What a curse, to be an island.

Someday, someway, somehow. That’s how it goes, right?

It’s cold in these waters
Though the sea is warm
And full of fish

What brings a fish to delight in the air?
Life, just a little longer.

poems.title: Today I Saw a Man on a Leash
stanzas:
Today I saw a man on a leash
Or maybe it was a woman on a leash
It was hard to tell which person was being held
And which person was being restrained

It was an elephant leash
Easily broken

And like an elephant’s leash
It came with a curious sense of misfortune

What addiction tricked you, big man (woman)
How did you (they) come to be tied with an elephant leash
In the forest, the elephant walks far more silently than the man.

poems.title: Today I Write About Red
stanzas:
Today I write about Red
(not Blue a color so close so dear to near heart I am not sure who I was before I met you)
But Red.
Its darker cousin.
Sister of Black.

Murderer of green into the turgid hell of Brown
Yes today I speak about Red
My beautiful sister.
I can’t wait to make purple once more.

poems.title: Today If There Is Tomorrow
stanzas:
Today if there is tomorrow
If there was a day it was tomorrow and if it was tomorrow, it was a day
Where did the birds go when the rains fall without end? Where do we go when we find our heart? Where do we go when we wonder about tomorrow?
Where do we go when our hearts quail from fright?
Where do we go when we wonder mystery and forget heart. Where do we go when we leave this life?
Into tomorrow, I say, and fight me if I’m wrong.

poems.title: Wedding Poem
stanzas:
Our story began in Sadashivnagar, under orange lights and in empty roads
A time when the land is very dry, the summer is yet to come, and the rains are yet to start
By April, we were found, in that brief wisp of spring,
that Bangalore gets, sometimes, somewhere, somehow.

After that, what is love, but a set of choices
made with a little more sparkle
a little more joy, maybe
a little more wonder, maybe

Thinking just
a few days
ahead
of where
you
used to think
before.

After that first year we thought,
“This is it!” Time to scurry home
And find our stories again
Don’t let fling become fantasy

And fantasy becomes a pale version of itself
When reality takes its bitter hold,
and mashes it beyond all understanding.

But somehow this reality never got mashed
these days are still like that first day
when we wondered was this fantasy
or is this a real life.
Just a real life we never imagined
a new, different kind of world

Telling any story takes choosing an arbitrary beginning and end
In a grand story that has no beginning and end
Especially stories that are about concepts that we made up
The grand delusions of abstract nouns
Like falling in love.

poems.title: When I Dance with You
stanzas:
When I dance with you
I don’t know where my body ends
And yours begins

I wonder
Is this the way I’m meant to be
Joined with another

Your breath is my breath
And your tomorrow is my tomorrow
Let us be conjoined, oh my sibilant lover

poems.title: When I Laugh
stanzas:
When I laugh
with you
There is this warm glow
i feel
that comes up from my tummy
and settles in a strange place
behind the lungs

Just there
pleasantly warm
Until I forget to think about it
anymore

And all that’s left is a memory
Of something pleasantly warm
On a cold day
Like chocolate
Simmered hot
With a few marshmallows
White clouds of goodness
In a dark brown sea.

poems.title: When I'm not here
stanzas:
When I'm not here
With you
I miss
The curve of your back
It's very satisfying
To hold
And pull towards me
After a bad dream

Or
Maybe
Not a dream at all

But a thing
That woke you up in the middle of the night
The way
That things to do
Now that we are adults
And sleep side by side

With a little gap
Most the time
Because sleeping well is hard
Much harder than it seemed
When we were doing it
Before

It's weird
Sometimes
Being the person
I aspired to be

But then I
Guess
You always
Saw me as that person

So it isn't as weird
Being that person
When I'm around you
Or something
Like
That

poems.title: When you watch the whales from shore
stanzas:
When you watch the whales from shore
There is a certainty. Anesthesia
Wonder
we

As you see the great plumps of white rise in the hosts by sea
And you Zer structure by how small those boats and humans see
And how huge and mighty whales must be.
Surrender to the powerful we are taught,
And surrender to the powerful we do, happily, frequently, habitually.

When you see them up close
Smell the breath
Realize the majesty
Is covered with rough
And this diamond cannot be polished
To be pleasing to our eye
Why then,
We kill them and eat them.
It's a good thing mother sea keeps our boats small.

poems.title: When You Were Young
stanzas:
When you were young
You got to try on different identities
To act, to play, to try this face with these people
To try to act like THIS at camp
To try to be, and be! In fact.

But me, you see, I was always Queer.
Sometimes Fag or It, or a hundred spiteful names.

But it took a long time. For me to claim a name or a face.
An identity just to be.
To try.
Like a game with some new friends.
For a few hours.
In the woods.
On a Saturday.

poems.title: Xoxo
stanzas:
Xoxo
How lucky am I;
To be surrounded by;
so much love,
We’d have conversations
(about picking and choosing)
whose love,
We’d rather keep.

poems.title: I came out
stanzas:
In the morning you can listen to the mist. It dies as it burns, little by little, slow by slow.

If you sit still and don’t move your eyes you can see it fleeing.

It runs from the invading sun, hoping, wondering,
Thinking maybe today, maybe this day, even if I don’t win, one of us will.

Their kiss is soft and cool on my skin, and tastes of a color I’ve never seen.

When I first came out I saw the drops of dew and wondered — is this? Will this be?

Then their bodies broke together, melded into ever bigger drops, and I remembered, oh, yes, this is the ocean, just come to play

in the air for a time.

poems.title: Being Loved
stanzas: There is a memory I have a day I once got lost. There have been times I have been truly lost, but this was not a time I was truly lost. This was a time that I was thought to be lost, not by myself, but by the context and situations that I existed in. In my mind, there was a moment of trying a new thing, of doing something fun, or going to go to chase a feeling. It is hazy the way that feelings are remembered in the chasing. It is hazy the way that memories are remembered in the after. I remember the swing. And swinging.

It had a creak, when it moved, especially as I got older. It told you that it was not the right age for you anymore. That this time had passed. That you had grown up to new things, to new experiences. That you no longer belonged here. But in this memory, the creak was still gentle. It was the grumble of the wood that was still doing its assigned purpose, not that groan of a tool at its capacity. The groan of something at the end of its line. The groan of despair, before the sharp break of failure. The creak was gentle.

It was a soft creak, and there was a soft breeze, the kind generated by a swing when there is no room for the air to grow its own strength. The kind generated when there are 4 walls that hover close and box the world in. That create safety through keeping out the untoward(s). And blocking the air. So the breeze could only be that made by artifice, by legs and weight, thrown against ropes, rubber paddle too stiff to sit. Comfortably sit. But maybe that’s an addition I make now, as I massage this memory and squeeze it for juice.

As I try to fill in the blanks that the moths of despair and desperation ate when they fought to keep us from falling into some hole, some place, some thing that seemed too much in that moment and ate the memories around it in its effort to ensure that this time, this lesson would not be forgotten –I look for anchors to tell me where this memory existed. Perhaps that moment that followed that glorious few forgotten moments of wonder on that swing ate those moments of glory. Hasn’t fear always eaten moments of glory? Hasn’t wonder always been subjugated by shame?

Shame came calling, when the world bore witness to my mother’s fear. Wonder, fear and the rush of warmth masquerading as joy as equilibrium drives to be restored when the cause célèbre has been rectified. Blessed we are when we are young, that the artifacts of these moments are swept up easily. Age leaves more and more notches and creases, places to gather detritus, harder for equilibrium to be restored.

Back door swung open and there she stood, so excited I was to have come to the backyard by myself, to have taken myself outside for a moment of safe adventure before my next feeding, before resuming the cycle of what must be done and what must follow what. Back door swung open and there she stood, so shocked, but so relieved, washed with such strong emotion there was nothing else in that moment. Do I invent this back door? Do I invent this moment of discovery? I probe and wonder — did I not just walk in that same door I dream swung open?

Could this memory of a mother so caught by shock she is wordless be real? Has there ever been any other moment — when struck by grief or worry, fear or wonder, anxiety or awe — that she has stood wordless? Say nay and say truth or say yay and continue to dream. The bus had been called, and the school, that is for certain. That shame I remembered, that I had caused, by signaling poorly my whereabouts.

That shame I remember, that it ate away the rest of it, the moments of glory, the moments of wonder, the moments of thinking that I was free to do as I pleased. That these walls could be bent. Or did it? Glass, uncolor my view, lead me back to what truth might I see.

poems.title: Animals in Love
stanzas:
I watch us eat a piece of meat.
We are a heathen revealed.

Base animal instincts.

Tearing at it with our hands.
Ripping the pieces off the bone.
It’s rip tear mouth chew.

Like a baby, almost. Or person made baby, by circumstance or situation.

Rip tear chew.
Repeat.

Repeat.

Repeat.

the meat, cold from the fridge; oil working its way out across the parchment paper and into the box, emblazoned with telltale marks of capitalism at work, branding for the day you find a box, half rotted behind some milk that was too big for the usual shelf and took up more than its allotted share, blocking the view until the putrid smell called for the investigation, the growth of indifference breeding, that will be the end of this box as the oil having soaked its way into the box cooly slicks surfaces and the meat is still cold as you
rip tear chew.
again.
again.
again.

Are you/we/us an animal?

Would that be so bad, to be an animal.

would it be erosion of the guardrails that made us great? The backpedaling of growth. The devolution of the higher form.

What is great?

Come watch water and in metamorphous see the nature of wonder. Is it a cloud I watch today. Or a stream. Or a body, a sack of water made mobile and self-healing. What form does water take in the void. Maybe its droplets fall to be ever smaller droplets.

One drop divided.

We’re in love until we’re not, amirite?

Quick, a game.
Who’s more sentient. You eating meat or me ripping flesh.

Who’s more sentient. You torn in my memory, or me chewed up in your heart.

Who’s more sentient. You that I dream eating, or me that you ripped apart.

Who’s more sentient. You who I knew, or me before you died.

poems.title: wrestle
stanzas:
I wrestle with these feelings of badness
I have done something wrong
My heart tells me
I have done something wrong
My short breath tells me
This pain
Along the sternum
Headed to the stomach and to the throat
Oily -seeming
Dark -feeling
(I have done something wrong)

But damn it does start to change
once it moves

Substance too thick congeals so dark
But beautifies to purple in the light

poems.title: Bladder bag
stanzas:
I, bladder bag, am made cold again, my secret inner fire being doused again, again, again, where did that warmth that surrounded me once go.
Who she this whale I once was disgorging my contents and purging my sisters to make a slop, what is this soup
She this whale I once was takes me with a soft hand, speaks gently, makes soft the water and stirs away the hard pieces that come of the night.
I am made cold and made warm, I, basti, am made anew, I am container of slop and holder of soup, I am reborn as bag.

poems.title: hey
stanzas:
hey, you there
hey
hey you here
we got stuck together somehow
your shoulder got caught in my shirt
your breath got caught in my air

*beat*
is that yours or is that mine

*beat*

hi
